title: Luckin Coffee — The Scandal That Didn’t End the Story
narration: A coffee company is opening stores at a breathtaking pace. Its app is offering discounts. Customers are ordering from their phones. Investors are watching it challenge Starbucks in China. Then investigators begin counting what is happening inside the stores. They record transactions. They collect receipts. They watch customer traffic. And the picture they assemble does not match the growth story investors have been told. Luckin Coffee would eventually admit that hundreds of millions of dollars in sales had been fabricated. Its shares collapsed. Its chairman and chief executive were removed. That sounds like the end of the company. It wasn’t. Luckin kept operating. It kept selling coffee. And after the scandal, it returned to growth. So the real story is not only how a coffee chain faked sales. It is how the fraud was exposed, what part of the business remained real, and how a company can outlive the story that once made it valuable.
